searchText: Much of team effort has been in improving block production. I wander if there has been an attempt to delay attestations in slot zero. Reports of users losing Gwei on slot zero started picking up on Discord channels. A good head+target vote outweighs the inclusion distance reward. What I would want to try is to delay waiting for the first block a few more seconds before submitting an attestation. These will most likely be included later, at the risk of not being included at all. But I would want to see a simulation of the economics of this setup. It should be simple to implement and test on pyrmont. Unfortunately to measure any impact I'd have to have many validators so the only ones that can effectively do this are the dev teams+EF. Is it a terribly bad idea? I suspect 1.2 seconds should be enough. 2 would certainly suffice Attestations aren't produced until the earlier of the block arriving or 4 seconds, are you suggesting delaying them additional 2 seconds (_i.e._ up to 6 seconds after the start of the epoch)? Yes I'd like to measure if the impact on inclusion distance of good attestations is more than the gain on good head+target vote Wouldn't be too hard to test, could be interesting to see the impact. I like the idea, but it's not configurable right now, so we would need to adjust it in client code. And then do a wide node update, amidst Christmas/new year holidays. Let's just wait till afterwards for non-urgent updates. The client devs deserve some rest :) 😂 sure, I do not know the other clients codebase, but I could easily send a patch for prysm, it's a one liner I think Yes, think the patch wouldn't be difficult. And I do like the idea. But updating a lot of nodes at the same time is not a good recipe for a nice holiday 😅 Oh yes, this reminds me Happy holidays to everyone! It could well have knock-on effects. Playing with it on pyrmont with local patches is probably a good place to start. <@!755590043632140352> this was from our topaz testnet days https://hackmd.io/dVbmIMHNQ6aby77g0-ME8A?both I hacked the validators to wait for 6s instead of 4s before sending out attestations. That brought up correctly voted head % from 85% to 97% Fantastic But i wander how that'll do now that block proposition is optimized, in theory clients are less prone to include late attestations
